title: Redwood x CeresCloud Partner Intro & Discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and CeresCloud to explore GTM collaboration and technical integration paths. Discussed dedicated vs hosted models, private/VPC options, security requirements (SOC2/KMS), and initial benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: share partner deck, run a small benchmark, and schedule a deeper technical workshop.
next_steps: Redwood to send partner deck and high-level commercial model by 2026-04-21
CeresCloud to share preferred SKUs and integration constraints by 2026-04-22
Schedule technical runbook/benchmark session (SE-led) for week of 2026-04-27

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Thompson (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood Partnerships), Lena Park (CeresCloud Head of Cloud Partnerships), Ibrahim Khan (CeresCloud Solutions Architect), Sofia Ruiz (CeresCloud BD)

Summary (auto): Quick partner intro, high-level architecture compatibility, security checklist, and benchmark pilot plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Ava from Redwood, I'm the AE on the partnership side. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lena Park: Hi Ava, good thanks. Lena here at CeresCloud. Happy to be on this call.
[00:09] Ibrahim Khan: Ibrahim, solutions. Afternoon.
[00:11] Marco Diaz: Marco, Redwood SE. Thanks for taking the time.
[00:13] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, BD at CeresCloud.
[00:15] Ava: Cool, quick agenda — intros, partner motion goals, high-level tech fit, security/compliance, and then next steps and action items. Any additions?
[00:23] Lena: That works. We'd like to also talk about SKUs and co-selling motions.
[00:27] Ava: Perfect. I'll hand it to Marco to walk through the technical surface area briefly.
[00:31] Marco: Sure, thanks. So Redwood provides a unified inference platform — hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem options. The key things we hear partners care about are: model compatibility, latency/cost tradeoffs, and how we integrate with partner infrastructure for things like private networking and KMS.
[00:48] Ibrahim: Quick question — when you say private VPC, is that a customer-managed VPC that your control plane talks to, or is it a fully isolated on-prem appliance?
[00:56] Marco: Good question. We have both options. For VPC deployments we provide a private control plane that you can configure to talk to customer-managed VPC endpoints. For fully air-gapped or regulated customers we offer an on-prem package. There are differences in telemetry and SLA surface.
[01:10] Ibrahim: Okay would the on-prem package require us to ship hardware or is it software you install?
[01:14] Marco: It's primarily a software bundle plus a minimum resource profile. We do provide recommended hardware SKUs and partner validated images, but we don't ship hardware in most cases. For tight integrations we do work with partners like Ceres to validate particular GPU SKUs.
[01:25] Lena: That aligns with what we wanted to hear. Our partners want flexibility — some enterprise accounts won't allow outbound control-plane connections.
[01:32] Marco: Right, and for those we typically recommend private deployments with customer-controlled networking and KMS integrations. Our key integration points are: SAML SSO, customer KMS via HSM/KMS APIs, audit logs, and per-request policy hooks.
[01:44] Ava: On the GTM side, we typically have three partner motions: resell/refer for hosted API, dedicated capacity co-sell, and private deployments for large enterprise. Curious where Ceres sees the most traction?
[01:56] Sofia: We've seen traction for dedicated and private with regulated customers — finance, healthcare. Also some smaller startups prefer the hosted model for quick onboarding.
[02:06] Lena: Yes and for our channel we care about predictable pricing on GPU SKUs, and we want a simple partner SOC/security packet.
[02:14] Marco: We have SOC 2 Type II, and we can share a security pack. We integrate with customer KMS for key management and our audit logs can be exported to partner SIEMs — usual stuff. There may be minor naming mismatches in the docs, sorry, we often have auto-gen naming in the exports.
[02:29] Ibrahim: Yeah, it's fine. On performance: can you talk about how you handle batching and KV cache so we can estimate latency on our GPU SKUs?
[02:37] Marco: Sure. We do continuous batching and KV cache optimizations. Kernel selection is dynamic based on model and sequence length distribution. For dedicated pools you can tune batching windows and concurrency; our runtime will suggest optimal configurations based on observed traffic. For cost optimization we recommend quantization profiles for some models.
[02:53] Ava: We can share typical perf profiles for models like Llama2-13B and Falcon variants, but final numbers depend on sequence length and batch mix.
[03:02] Ibrahim: Understood. What about multi-tenant isolation in dedicated pools? Do you guarantee tenant-level QoS?
[03:08] Marco: For dedicated we provide capacity isolation at the GPU pool level — you get reserved capacity. If you need hard tenant-level QoS within a shared pool we can look at resource limits and quotas, but the cleanest is reserved pools.
[03:20] Sofia: SKUs — can we get recommended GPU types? We've been seeing customer asks for H100 and A100.
[03:26] Marco: H100 is preferred for large models and highest throughput, A100 is still common for cost-sensitive workloads. We also support Ampere variants and can work with partners on optimized kernels for newer chipsets.
[03:36] Lena: On the integration timeline, typically how long from initial POC to GA for a private deployment?
[03:42] Marco: It varies. For a benchmark + PoC with a partner-validated image, typically 4–8 weeks if networking/permissions are straightforward. On-prem takes longer because of procurement and hardware lead times.
[03:52] Ava: On compliance — customers often ask about residency and audit logs. We can provide logs and retention policies and work with partner SIEMs. We'll share our SOC2 report and an overview of what fields are logged.
[04:03] Lena: Good. Do you support per-tenant encryption with external KMS? Some enterprise customers require that.
[04:08] Marco: Yes we integrate with external KMS and HSM providers. You can bring your own keys and we never store unencrypted key material.
[04:15] Ibrahim: Network egress — for hosted customers, is there a way to keep traffic inside the partner backbone (e.g., private peering) to meet data residency?
[04:24] Marco: For Dedicated we can work on private peering and region pinning. For hosted we have region-based endpoints but private peering is more of a partner-level arrangement.
[04:33] Sofia: From a GTM perspective, what does success look like? Co-sell opportunities? Joint customers? Revenue share?
[04:39] Ava: All of the above are on the table. Our partnership models include referral fees for hosted, joint-resell for Dedicated, and co-selling for Private deployments. We can go more into specifics once we have a partner profile and expected deal sizes.
[04:52] Lena: Can you share an example MSA or partner agreement?
[04:54] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we have a standard partner addendum and a reseller MSA template. I'll share it. Note that legal tweaks are common.
[05:01] Ibrahim: Benchmarks — can we run a small benchmark with one of our SKUs? We'd like to see latency and token cost comparisons.
[05:07] Marco: Absolutely. Typical benchmark flow: partner provides an environment or we spin up a dedicated test pool on Ceres SKUs, run a set of workloads (LLM gen, embeddings, chat), and produce a perf+cost report. We usually need a test data set and expected percentiles to measure.
[05:21] Lena: We'll assemble a short workload — can you provide a sample config and any Docker/AMI we should use?
[05:25] Marco: Yes, I'll send the runbook and reference AMI/config. We also have a short benchmark spreadsheet with cost calculations.
[05:32] Ava: Quick note: some partner customers will insist on private networking or no outbound — that typically adds a week or two to setup for control-plane handshakes and IAM.
[05:41] Ibrahim: Noted. For the private deployment, how do you handle updates and patching if the customer's environment is air-gapped?
[05:47] Marco: For air-gapped setups we provide release bundles and a patch plan. Patching cadence is agreed during the onboarding; we provide signed artifacts and upgrade instructions.
[05:56] Sofia: Licensing/price — is there a minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[05:59] Ava: Yes, Dedicated usually has a reserved commit — monthly or annual commits based on GPU capacity. We can be flexible depending on the partner arrangement for pilots.
[06:10] Lena: Good to hear. Any regulatory certs beyond SOC2 you support or plan to?
[06:15] Marco: We support SOC2 Type II currently. For customers that need ISO or HIPAA support we have controls and processes; HIPAA requires additional BAAs and some private deployment constraints, so that tends to be focused on Private deployments.
[06:29] Ibrahim: How about observability — do you expose per-route traces and token-level billing?
[06:33] Marco: Yes, our console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, and tracing hooks so partners and customers can correlate requests end-to-end.
[06:44] Ava: Let's talk obstacles — from our side the main ones are certification (SOC2/ISO), pricing clarity on SKUs, and an easy benchmark flow. From Ceres side?
[06:53] Lena: For us it's proving performance on our SKUs, agreeing on a partner commercial model, and ensuring private networking options for enterprise customers.
[07:02] Sofia: Also enablement — joint playbooks and a partner-facing portal would help.
[07:07] Priya: We have partner enablement assets; we'll collaborate on a co-branded playbook once we know the motion.
[07:12] Ibrahim: A couple technical gotchas — some of our customers use strict egress rules and require DNS/IP allowlists. How does Redwood handle that?
[07:21] Marco: We support IP allowlists and can provide static egress endpoints for private deployments. Hosted has ephemeral endpoints but regionally pinned.
[07:31] Lena: Timeline again — if we start a pilot next week, can we have results in two weeks?
[07:36] Marco: For a small pilot with a validated image and accessible networking, two weeks is achievable for perf numbers. Onboarding the private VPC or air-gapped will push that out.
[07:47] Ava: Great — let's capture concrete next steps.
[07:50] Ava: Action item recap: Ava will share partner deck and pricing; Marco will share benchmark runbook and AMI; Lena will share SKUs and sample workload. Priya will share partner legal templates.
[08:01] Lena: Sounds good. We'll also try to identify an initial joint pilot customer.
[08:05] Sofia: I'll work with BD to identify candidates and loop them in.
[08:09] Ibrahim: I'll coordinate on the environment and networking constraints.
[08:12] Marco: One more note — some kernel-level performance differences show up on newer silicon; if you want we can run a micro-benchmark suite to help pick optimal drivers and CUDA versions.
[08:22] Ibrahim: Please do, that would help.
[08:24] Ava: Okay wrapping up — thanks everyone for the time. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the SE-led benchmark session.
[08:32] Lena: Thanks all.
[08:33] Sofia: Thanks!
[08:34] Priya: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
